news.title: ‘Don’t Waste Flamingos’ World Cup Triumph’ –Sodje Tasks NFF, NSC
news.lede: Former Super Eagles defender Sam Sodje has urged the National Sports Commission (NSC) and the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) to closely track and nurture the development of the Flamingos following their triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Sodje warned that Nigeria could end up wasting the landmark victory if the young champions are abandoned once the celebrations die down, rather than being given a clear, structured pathway into professional football. news.title: Serengeti Boys fight back to hold Costa Rica in World Cup opener
news.lede: Tanzania’s Under-17 national football team, the Serengeti Boys, made an impressive statement on their FIFA U-17 World Cup debut after recovering from a two-goal deficit to force a 2-2 draw against Costa Rica in their opening Group I match. Striker Faraji Kayanda emerged as Tanzania’s hero, scoring twice in the second half to rescue a valuable point for the debutants at Aspire Zone in Doha, Qatar. The result offered a strong response from head coach Elieneza Nsanganzelu’s youngsters, who looked in danger of suffering a difficult start to their maiden appearance at the global competition after conceding twice within the opening 15 minutes. Costa Rica took the lead in the eighth minute through Jefrey Urbina, who capitalised on an opportunity to put his side ahead and immediately increase the pressure on the Tanzanian youngsters.

news.title: Björkegren Names 23-Player Black Queens Squad for 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup Play-Offs
news.lede: Black Queens head coach Kim Lars Björkegren has named a 23-player squad for Ghana’s crucial preliminary campaign in the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 Play-Off Tournament, scheduled to take place in Rabat, Morocco, from November 28 to December 5, 2026. Ghana will be aiming to secure a place in the final phase of the intercontinental play-offs as they pursue a return to the FIFA Women’s World Cup for the first time since their last appearance in 2007. Experienced captain Portia Boakye headlines the squad, which features a blend of established internationals, foreign-based players and domestic league prospects. Key players such as Grace Asantewaa, Jennifer Cudjoe, Evelyn Badu and Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah are also included, providing Björkegren with considerable experience and quality across the various departments.

news.title: Black Challenge to face Morocco in final of 2026 Amputee World Cup
news.lede: The Black Challenge held their nerve to secure a 4-3 win on penalties following a 1-1 draw after extra time, moving within one win of claiming their maiden world title. The two sides played out a goalless 50 minutes of regulation time before Ghana broke the deadlock nine minutes into extra time. Tournament top scorer Mohammed Mubarik converted from the penalty spot to give the Black Challenge the lead and take his tally to seven goals. Ghana’s advantage was short-lived, however, as Türkiye fought back to restore parity in extra time and force the match into a penalty shootout.

news.title: Lionel Messi’s 2022 World Cup Final masterclass: The night he completed football
news.lede: For Lionel Messi, the 2022 FIFA World Cup final was about more than lifting the one trophy that had eluded him. It was the completion of a career filled with extraordinary achievements, individual records and heartbreaking near-misses on the international stage. On December 18, 2022, at the Lusail Stadium in Qatar, Messi finally got his moment. In a dramatic final against France, he scored twice, helped Argentina through extra time and converted his penalty in the shootout as the South American side won their third World Cup.

news.title: Amputee football: Morocco come from behind to beat Brazil and reach World Cup final
news.lede: Morocco's amputee football team are continuing their exceptional run at the 2026 World Cup. After falling behind, the Atlas Lions fought back to beat Brazil 2-1 on Friday in the semi-finals in Mexico and book their place in the final. A victory full of character that moves them closer to a first world title. Rieltony LOUBOKO · Author profile · 21/11/2026 08:22 UTC.

news.title: Ghana’s national amputee team stun defending champions Türkiye to reach historic football World Cup final
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge have booked a historic first-ever place in the final of the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup after defeating defending champions Türkiye 4-3 on penalties following a 1-1 draw after extra time in their semi-final in Mexico, after overcoming an early group-stage setback and successive knockout challenges. Ghana and Türkiye were goalless in regulation time before tournament-leading scorer Mohammed Mubarik converted a penalty nine minutes into extra time, after his effort in the box was handled. It was his seventh goal of the competition and his fifth consecutive match on the scoresheet. Disaster however struck Ghana after hardworking midfielder Hamza Mohammed received a red card moments after the Black Challenge scored, handing the opponents a vital numerical advantage.
